member.name: T:ExxerCube.Prisma.Infrastructure.Calendar.MexicoBusinessDayCalculator
member.summary: Holiday-aware business-day calculator for Mexico, backed by the PublicHoliday package's which tracks Mexican federal holidays as defined by the Ley Federal del Trabajo.

remarks.para: Both and delegate to the PublicHoliday package methods, which skip weekends (Saturday/Sunday) AND recognised Mexican federal public holidays (1 Jan, 5 Feb, 21 Mar, 1 May, 16 Sep, 18 Nov, 25 Dec, etc.).

uses an exclusive end convention consistent with the existing SLAEnforcerService.CalculateBusinessDays(start, end) semantics (exclusive-end). Note: MexicoPublicHoliday.BusinessDaysBetween counts both endpoints inclusively, so the wrapper subtracts 1 when the end date itself is a working day.
The instance is thread-safe and stateless beyond the year it is queried for; a single shared instance per calculator is sufficient.

member.name: M:ExxerCube.Prisma.Infrastructure.Calendar.MexicoBusinessDayCalculator.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of using the default configuration (federal holidays, no state-specific variants).

member.name: M:ExxerCube.Prisma.Infrastructure.Calendar.MexicoBusinessDayCalculator.AddBusinessDays(System.DateTime,System.Int32)
member.remarks: Delegates to MexicoPublicHoliday.BusinessDaysAdd(startDate, businessDays), which skips weekends and Mexican federal holidays. Passing zero returns unchanged.

remarks.para: The contract uses an exclusive end convention: itself is never counted. This matches the behaviour of SLAEnforcerService.CalculateBusinessDays(start, end) whose loop condition is while (currentDate < endDate).

The underlying MexicoPublicHoliday.BusinessDaysBetween method counts both endpoints inclusively. This wrapper corrects for that by subtracting 1 when itself is a working day, so the two implementations remain semantically equivalent.
